gaps.wanted: An elevation in the STAGED documents. The DCS201's guide has an Overview with both faces drawn across half a page each; this one has no Overview at all, so the only full-panel art in the staged corpus is the package-contents thumbnail on page 1 - both faces stacked, beside the bracket kit, at 3.22 px/mm and in perspective. THE FRONT IS NO LONGER BLOCKED BY THIS: the vendor's own square-on product photograph (DCS202-F) supplied the anchor the thumbnail could not, and Gate 1 passes on it at 1.1%. The REAR still rests on the thumbnail plus the DCS201's proven carry-over, and a rear photograph or elevation would let it be measured directly rather than inherited.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Nothing in this corpus draws any of them flat; the mounting figures show the lid and one side in three-quarter view while brackets go on, which shows nothing is printed there and gives nothing to model. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md - empty by verification, not by omission.

The individual centres of the twenty-four lane boxes. The label strip carries the same six bracketed groups of four the DCS201 has, and at 3.22 px/mm the groups resolve but the boxes inside them do not. They are therefore MAPPED from the DCS201's measured grid onto this device's own columns - x = 27.95 + (x201 - 32.78) x 13.97/14.25, which is the two walls' anchors and pitches - rather than read off this figure. The count, the bracket labels and which port each names are read here; the millimetres are constructed.
  I TRIED SCALING THEM AND GATE 5 DISPROVED IT. The first construction mapped the DCS201's
  grid onto this device's narrower columns - x = 27.95 + (x201 - 32.78) x 13.97/14.25 -
  on the assumption that the legend tracks the port pitch. Put beside the reference at
  matched scale that put every group about 8 mm left of where it is drawn. The legend does
  NOT track the wall: this device's first bracket starts at roughly 163.5 where the
  DCS201's measured 163.82, so the strip is printed at the same absolute place on both
  faces. The DCS201's measured grid is therefore used unshifted, which is a borrowing with
  one checked anchor rather than an arithmetic guess.

An elevation of the DC supply, which this corpus lacks exactly as the DCS201's does. The part it seats, edgecore/dcs201-psu-dc@1, already records that its face comes from a three-quarter figure; nothing here improves on it.

gate-1.note: FAILS ON THE ASPECT, AND WORSE THAN THE DCS201's DID. The front reads 1425 px wide on a face whose drawn height is nothing like 1/10.07 of that, because this is the same kind of perspective render as the sibling's and at 3.22 px/mm rather than 5.06 - the whole device is a thumbnail beside a picture of the bracket kit. The top cover is drawn above the face and the face is foreshortened. SO THE VERTICAL IS NOT USED AT ALL and the horizontal is used only where the ruler and the thing measured sit at the same height. That is the same split the DCS201 made, for the same reason, with less resolution to spend.

gate-5.note: I PUT THE MODEL OVER THE REFERENCE AT MATCHED SCALE, AND HERE IS WHAT IT SHOWED. Not the render beside the photograph - the two have very different textures and comparing them by eye misled me three times - but the MODEL'S OWN COLUMN CENTRES drawn as ticks onto the orthographic photograph at 6x. All twenty-four ticks land on jack centres across the full wall, and both predicted block gaps fall inside their dividers: the first is predicted at 142.53 mm against a wall pair straddling 142.4 in the photograph, and column 17's left bezel wall is predicted at 262.25 against 262.59 measured. THE REAR IS CHECKED THE SAME WAY, against this device's own orthographic rear photograph (DCS202-B). Its five red fan handles centre at 102.22, 161.28, 220.34, 278.95 and 338.46 mm against the model's carried 103.60, 162.42, 221.24, 280.06 and 338.88 - five modules inside 1.4 mm - and an edge scan puts the supplies' frames at 16.36-69.06 and 369.81-423.42 against the carried 16.74 and 371.37 at 54.0 wide. Every difference is inside this photograph's own 0.9 mm per pixel.

lamps.note: quick start, Connect Network Cables, verbatim: "For the RJ-45 ports: Green - 10 Gbps mode, Amber - 1 Gbps mode"; its table of the four link LEDs on each QSFP28 port, transcribed: 100 Gbps = 1 lamp green; 40 Gbps = 1 blue; 25 Gbps breakout (four lanes) = 1-4 amber; 10 Gbps breakout (four lanes) = 1-4 purple. Verify Switch Operation adds "the PSU1/PSU2, OS Diag, and Fan LEDs should all be on green". ONE LAMP PER QSFP PORT IS DRAWN rather than four, the same simplification the DCS201 and edgecore/as5912-54x make, because the art does not resolve four windows at 3.22 px/mm.

power.note: datasheet and quick start: "323 Watts maximum" for the chassis, against two 400 W supplies, so one supply carries the box and the second is redundant.

sources.note: Two documents, both staged and both docling-converted, MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGE. dcs202-datasheet (the DCS202 / AS5835-54T data sheet) holds the specification tables and a photographic product shot; dcs202-qsg (the AS5835-54T Quick Start Guide) holds the panel art. THIS GUIDE IS MUCH THINNER THAN ITS SIBLING'S - 59 figures against the DCS201's 108, and it has NO Overview section at all. It goes from Package Contents straight to installation, so the only full-panel drawing in the whole corpus is the package-contents thumbnail on page 1, which shows the front and the rear stacked. AND THE DECISIVE SOURCE IS NEITHER DOCUMENT. `working/intake/edgecore/photos/` holds dcs202-2-DCS202-F.png and dcs202-3-DCS202-B.png, the vendor's own square-on product photographs of both faces, staged by the intake alongside the PDFs. They are small - 489 x 357, about 1.1 px/mm on the panel - but they are ORTHOGRAPHIC, which is the property this device's guide lacks, and they are what Gate 1 and Gate 5 are taken against here. It also carries the family disclaimer: "The switch drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular switch model."

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 2 QSFP pairs (port-49/port-50 and port-52/port-53).

the-anchor-and-what-settled-it.note: THE WALL'S ANCHOR CAME FROM A SQUARE-ON PHOTOGRAPH, NOT FROM THE GUIDE. This device was first written as a draft because the guide's only full-panel art is a perspective thumbnail at 3.22 px/mm, and two bands of it put column 1 at 27.95 mm and at 37.7 - nearly a whole pitch apart - with no way to tell which feature each band was detecting. The vendor's own product photograph (DCS202-F, edge-core.com) is ORTHOGRAPHIC and settles it. Its face measures 488 x 49 px for an aspect of 9.959 against the stated 10.068, 1.1% out, so Gate 1 passes on it. Fitting the full 24-column model to the jack rows - registry pitch, gang 8, anchor and gutter free - gives column 1 at 35.25 mm and a 5.0 gutter at correlation 0.673, with the top six fits all inside 0.5 mm of each other. AND IT EXPLAINS THE CONTRADICTION. The guide band that read 41.92, 56.05, 70.02 was detecting the BRIGHT BEZEL WALLS BETWEEN columns, not the columns: subtract the half pitch of 6.985 and it reads 34.94, which is the photograph's answer to 0.3 mm. The other band was the same walls on the other side. Neither candidate was right and both were the same mistake. SO THE GUIDE'S FINER DATA IS USABLE AFTER ALL, once shifted. Its block C walls put column 17 at 269.23 where the model predicts 269.22, and its block B gives a 5.30 gutter against the photograph's 5.0. The anchor is the photograph's, the fine structure is the guide's, and the two agree across the whole wall.

the-breakout-legend.note: PRESENT, AND CARRIED IN STRUCTURE RATHER THAN IN POSITION. The label strip prints the same six bracketed groups of four numbered lane boxes the DCS201 has, one per QSFP28 port. At 3.22 px/mm the boxes resolve as a row of marks but their individual centres do not, so they are placed on this device's own measured column grid - each group sitting under the columns the drawing puts it under - rather than by reading twenty-four box centres the figure cannot give. The count, the bracket labels and which ports they name are read; the millimetres are constructed.

the-jacks-are-lamped-and-the-management-.note: THE SAME SPLIT AS THE SIBLING, AND HERE IT PUTS MOST PORTS ON THE LAMPED PART. The traffic jacks are Ethernet and light: "For the RJ-45 ports: Green - 10 Gbps mode, Amber - 1 Gbps mode", which is the pair of bezel lamps common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 draws, so all 48 take it and L76 is satisfied without argument. THE TWO MANAGEMENT JACKS DO NOT. Their label strip prints "MGMT" between an up and a down arrow with two plain windows beneath it and "On = link / Flash = ACT" beside them - the lamps are in the strip, not in the bezel - so those two take the BARE ganged part and their lamps are placed where the metal puts them, exactly as on the DCS201.

the-rear-is-carried-over-and-proven.note: CARRIED FROM edgecore/dcs201, AND THEN CHECKED AGAINST THIS DEVICE'S OWN FIGURE. The programme's rule is that an inherited number is marked carried over rather than measured; this one is both, because the check passed. The five honeycomb grilles in the DCS202's own rear thumbnail centre at 102.82, 161.72, 220.94, 280.00 and 338.91 mm, against the DCS201's 103.6, 162.5, 221.4, 280.1 and 338.9 - five modules agreeing to 0.78, 0.78, 0.46, 0.10 and 0.01 mm, and a bay pitch of 59.02 against 58.82, 0.3% apart. Two figures in two documents drawn for two devices landing inside a millimetre is what makes this a carry and not a guess. AND CONFIRMED A THIRD TIME by this device's own orthographic rear photograph, which puts its fan handles on a 59.06 pitch against the DCS201's 58.82 and its supplies' frames within 1.6 mm of the carried positions. THE CARRIED NUMBERS ARE KEPT RATHER THAN REPLACED BY THAT PHOTOGRAPH, deliberately: the DCS201's rear was read off a half-page elevation at 5.02 px/mm and the photograph is 1.1, so the carry is the more precise of the two and the photograph is the check on it. Swapping in coarser numbers because they are this device's own would trade accuracy for provenance tidiness. THE ARRANGEMENT IS IDENTICAL TOO: a supply at each end with a C14 inlet, a wire bail handle and a coloured latch, five honeycomb fan trays between them with pull bars and airflow diamonds, and the grounding screw outboard of the left-hand supply.

the-same-supplies-and-the-same-fan.note: THE SPECIFICATION TABLES ARE WORD FOR WORD. This guide's AC PSU section reads "100-240 VAC, 50-60 Hz, 400 Watts" with the breakdown "100-127 VAC, 47-63 Hz, 6.0 A / 200-240 VAC, 47-63 Hz, 3.0 A", and its 48 VDC PSU section reads "48 VDC, 400 Watts" and "-36 - -75 VDC, 14-7 A". Those are the DCS201's figures character for character, the faces drawn are the same faces, and the bays measure the same. So this device seats edgecore/dcs201-psu-ac@1, edgecore/dcs201-psu-dc@1 and edgecore/dcs201-fan@1 rather than copies of them under a second name. The parts carry a shared-with key recording that.

the-x-axis-is-measured.note: The RJ-45 wall's own pitch is the ruler. The lower row of jack openings resolves as 24 clean bright boxes whose steps read 13.97 mm against std/rj45-ganged@2's registry pitch of 13.97 - a lookup from a TE magjack CAD, not a measurement - agreeing to two decimal places across twenty-one of the twenty-three steps. THREE ANCHORS, EACH CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN EIGHT COLUMNS. Block A's first column centres at 41.92, block B's ninth at 159.14 and block C's seventeenth at 276.21. One block with gang 8 and a 5.46 gutter puts the seventeenth at 276.36, which is 0.15 mm from where it is drawn, so all twenty-four columns follow from three readings and a registry constant.

the-y-axis-is-derived.note: NOT MEASURED. The rows sit at 3.0 and 15.1, which is the ~12.1 mm belly-to-belly spacing std/rj45-ganged@2's registry notes record from the TE 2497310-1 CAD, started at the 3.0 mm top margin this vendor's 1RU faces use and edgecore/as5912-54x already carries. The wall then ends at 26.1 and leaves 17.9 mm for the label strip and the bottom vent, which is the proportion the drawing shows. None of it is a reading.
